segments.text: Start from the concrete action of exchanging rows and ask how a matrix could perform that operation.
Use a permutation matrix example. Run the multiplication line by line and check which row moves to each output position.
Compare multiplying on the left with multiplying on the right: one permutes rows while the other permutes columns.
Turn a matrix across its diagonal to build the transpose, then give the formal entry rule only after the visual picture.
Ask what happens when a product is transposed. Check a small example before stating that the multiplication order reverses.
Generalize vectors to R n, summarize the notation, and use a counterexample to separate row vectors from column vectors.
